title: What Perfume Making Studies — Fundamentals of Perfume Making
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Perfume Making Studies as part of the fundamentals of perfume making, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Foundations tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of perfume making, What Perfume Making Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Top notes means the first impression, citrus and herbs that fade fast Accord means a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Top notes: the first impression, citrus and herbs that fade fast
Accord: a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials
key_laws: Build in ratios and write everything down.
vocabulary: Sillage: the scent trail a perfume leaves
Parfum: the highest concentration, 20-30%
methods: Accord method: blend 3 materials on blotters at set ratios until balanced
history: Perfumery was refined in Grasse, France from the 1700s; modern hobby perfumery grew with access to aroma materials and the natural-perfume movement of the 2000s.
key_points: Top notes: the first impression, citrus and herbs that fade fast
Accord: a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials
Key vocabulary: Sillage — the scent trail a perfume leaves; Parfum — the highest concentration, 20-30%.
Governing principle: Build in ratios and write everything down.
how_it_works: The Signature learner approaches What Perfume Making Studies by anchoring it to what is already known: Sillage (the scent trail a perfume leaves), then Parfum (the highest concentration, 20-30%). The working method is Accord method: blend 3 materials on blotters at set ratios until balanced Practice means rehearsing the idea until it can be reconstructed from scratch, which is exactly what the accompanying study program drills.

name: The Future of Perfume Making — perfume making fundamentals record
title: The Future of Perfume Making — Fundamentals of Perfume Making
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches The Future of Perfume Making as part of the fundamentals of perfume making, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Advanced tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of perfume making, The Future of Perfume Making is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Accord means a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials Blotters means paper strips for testing without skin chemistry interference Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Accord: a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials
Blotters: paper strips for testing without skin chemistry interference
key_laws: Rest blends before judging; fresh mixes lie.
Test on skin last; paper lies about longevity.
vocabulary: Longevity: how long the scent lasts on skin
Eau de parfum: 15-20% concentration
methods: Build method: compose top, heart, and base accords, then blend the accords
history: Perfumery was refined in Grasse, France from the 1700s; modern hobby perfumery grew with access to aroma materials and the natural-perfume movement of the 2000s.
key_points: Accord: a balanced mini-blend of two or three materials
Blotters: paper strips for testing without skin chemistry interference
Key vocabulary: Longevity — how long the scent lasts on skin; Eau de parfum — 15-20% concentration.
Governing principle: Rest blends before judging; fresh mixes lie.
how_it_works: The Signature learner approaches The Future of Perfume Making by anchoring it to what is already known: Longevity (how long the scent lasts on skin), then Eau de parfum (15-20% concentration). The working method is Build method: compose top, heart, and base accords, then blend the accords Practice means rehearsing the idea until it can be reconstructed from scratch, which is exactly what the accompanying study program drills.
requirements: Reader needs no prior background: every term used here is defined in this entry or in the Foundations tier entries before it.
standards: Standard curricula, textbooks, and professional references for perfume making.
provenance: Signature-authored fundamentals written for the JAH Signature system; speculative or interpretive content is Signature-labeled.
licensing: Public facts; original presentation. Property of Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
